sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Potsdam has priced its inner city up and is slowly removing street spaces. A 2017 inner-city traffic concept counted about 1,400 on-street spaces in the shopping centre, found that on-street demand generally exceeded legal supply, and noted that the Luisenplatz garage was often full while the Hegelallee garage usually had free capacity [3]. In June 2022 the council made Parkzone 1 in the inner city €3.00 an hour, up from €2, and merged the lower zones into Parkzone 2 at €1.50. The city said the aim was to steer drivers to peripheral garages priced at €1.50 to €2.50 an hour [5][6]. A proposal to raise Zone 2 to €2.00 was due to be voted on in December 2025, and we do not know the outcome [12]. Resident permits were €30 a year until the council set a fee of €145 for one year, or €275 for two, from 1 September 2025 [9][10]. Resident zones in Babelsberg were extended from 30 June 2025 [11].

The inner-city concept 'Straßenräume neu denken', adopted in May 2023, aims to reduce car traffic and especially parked cars. A one-year trial in Dortustraße from March 2024 removed the visitor and resident spaces in one section [7], and in March 2025 the city announced the trial result, with one section permanently traffic-calmed and parking prohibited in another except for two disabled and five short-term spaces [8]. At Park Sanssouci, a threatened entrance fee was averted for now when the state said it would cover the missing €800,000 a year to the palaces foundation [13].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Park-and-ride is the area with the most change. Paid-parking management at P+R Bahnhof Pirschheide started on 15 December 2024. The lot stays free for public-transport customers, and the city said about 80% of its use before had been by non-P+R users [14]. A city presentation of March 2025 lists the milestones, with management of Pirschheide done, Golm and Campus Jungfernsee to follow, and a concept for 10 sites in the city [15]. From 2 February 2026 cars may park at Campus Jungfernsee only with a valid local public-transport ticket [16].

In the centre, Contipark took over the Hegelallee 'Zentrum' garage, with 475 spaces, in mid-2026 and cut the first hour by €1.00 to €2.50 and the daily maximum from €35 to €20 [17]. Contipark's Luisenplatz garage has 278 spaces on the operator's page and 20 charging points [18]. APCOA runs the two Hauptbahnhof garages, with 1,041 and 351 spaces, from €1.50 an hour up to €12 a day, and the Filmpark Babelsberg garage with 957 spaces [19]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Potsdam data cover eight car parks with 1,359 spaces. Four are park-and-ride lots (454 spaces) more than 2 km out, and the others are the Hegelallee garage (470), the Luisenplatz garage (213 in our feed, 278 on the operator's page), the small Wilhelmgalerie (52) and Park Sanssouci's P2 lot (170). Contipark's Luisenplatz garage charges €3.50 an hour and €20 a day [18], more than twice APCOA's station rate [19].

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 53% on weekdays and 50% at weekends. The Hegelallee garage is the fullest, at 77% on weekdays and 86% at weekends, which is after the July price cut [17]. It averaged only 16% in 2025, and 32% over 2026 so far. The two car parks within 500 m of Brandenburger Straße, Hegelallee and the small Wilhelmgalerie, average 72%, against 33% for the four park-and-ride lots. Sanssouci P2 is busier on weekdays (61%) than at weekends (32%). Pirschheide, at 54%, averaged 70% in 2022, 45% in 2024 and 34% in 2025, the year after management began, and 45% in 2026 so far. The Marquardt lot is almost empty (6%). The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ.
